text: A Fado Evening
Fado, Alfama BLU Journey No. 104 Edition No. 05/2026 Journeys in Cities
Fado is not sung, it happens. — Amália Rodrigues, the queen of Fado.

Fado is not performed for the room. It is carried through it. Born in Lisbon, it reflects a way of feeling shaped by absence, longing, and memory. Silence is part of the experience. Conversations pause. Lights soften. The music is not explained, it is felt. Fado is often associated with saudade, a word that holds longing without resolution. Not sadness, but awareness. It is less about performance, and more about presence. Fado

A theater performance inspired by one of Portugal's most iconic musical traditions. Presented in a theatre setting, it combines music, voice, and visual storytelling in a contemporary interpretation of Fado. Rather than recreating the atmosphere of a traditional Fado house, it presents Fado in a contemporary stage format in the heart of Lisbon. Fado on Stage Why it stays with you Music at the center Music and visual storytelling A light evening experience

Lisbonʼs oldest quarter settles differently at night. Light settles along the walls. Voices lower. The streets narrow into silence. Fado belongs here. It grew within these houses, in informal gatherings and small taverns, where music was shared rather than performed. Walking through Alfama in the evening is part of the experience. Alfama at night Why it stays with you The narrow streets under evening light A neighborhood carried through time The quiet before the first note

Fado Dinner In Alfama, near the cathedral, this Fado restaurant remains faithful to the tradition. The room is intimate. Tables are close. The focus stays on the voice and the guitar. Dinner pauses as the music begins. There is no separation between stage and table. A place where Fado is respected, not adapted.
A few dishes that reflect the local table.
Caldo verde Potato cream soup, slices of kale, a slice of sausage. A simple and comforting beginning.
Codfish Clube de Fado style Oven-roasted cod loin, potatos and greens A classic Portuguese dish.
Croaker and shrimp cataplana (for 2 people) Mild white fish and shrimp, cooked in a traditional pan called cataplana with tomato, garlic, and white wine A regional specialty from the south.
Octopus lagareiro style Roasted octopus with olive oil, garlic, and potatoes. A personal favorite.
Portuguese style beef medallion Fried medallion, seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic in white wine and olive oil sauce. A familiar and reliable choice.
Leek Brás Style Leeks gently mixed with eggs and crispy potato strips. A traditional recipe, adapted for vegetarians.
Abade de Priscos Pudding A rich egg-yolk pudding with a subtle note of bacon and Port wine. A traditional dessert with depth and character.

Fado Show €25 per person complimentary for kids under 6 years old. Approximately 50 minutes. Shows everyday at 5.30pm and 7.30 pm. Includes reserved seating and a traditional fado performance accompanied by Portuguese guitar. INVESTMENT Fado Dinner €90 per person €45 per child 7-12 years old Complimentary for kids under 6 years old. Includes couvert, starter, main course, dessert, and two drinks.

At 09 a.m., we depart from Lisbon. Driving from Lisbon to Nazaré is a scenic journey that takes you through the heart of Portugal's stunning coastal landscape. The trip starts with a smooth ride on the A8 highway, leaving the bustling city of Lisbon behind as you head north. Along the way, you’ll pass rolling hills dotted with quaint villages and vineyards, showcasing the charm of rural Portugal. As you approach Nazaré, the Atlantic Ocean comes into view, its vast blue expanse hinting at the seaside adventures to come. Upon arrival, the sound of crashing waves and the sight of Nazaré’s famous towering cliffs welcome you, setting the stage for a memorable visit to this charming fishing town known for its giant waves and vibrant culture. L U N C H , 1 2 p . m .

After lunch, time to head towards Porto. But before, we have a quick stop to see the traditional way of drying fish in Nazaré. At the beaches of Nazaré, rows of sardines are traditionally laid out to dry under the warm Portuguese sun. Women in colorful skirts and headscarves carefully arrange the freshly caught fish on wooden racks, a method passed down through generations. The salty sea breeze adds a distinctive flavor to the sardines, creating a unique delicacy that reflects the town's deep connection to the sea. As the fish dry, they turn a silvery shade, shimmering in the sunlight and drawing the eyes of passersby who pause to admire this time-honored practice along the picturesque shoreline. As you wander, traces of time appear quietly in the streets, the façades, and the way the town continues to live around its history. text: CABO DA ROCA Cabo da Roca is a place where the land seems to pause before meeting the ocean, standing at the westernmost point of continental Europe. Here, wind, sea, and sky take the lead, offering a moment of presence where words feel unnecessary. Why it stays with you The feeling of standing at the edge The openess of the horizon Its raw beauty

A Journey Where Every Bite Reveals a Story Get ready for a sensory journey through Lisbon’s historic center, where every corner holds a memory and every flavor reveals centuries of tradition. Over the course of four hours, we invite you to dive into the soul of Portuguese gastronomy through century-old shops and beloved local institutions that preserve the true essence of our culture. Inside a Historic House of Portuguese Flavors Pick-up at the hotel or meeting point. Our first stop is a landmark deli from the 1800s and the perfect place to understand the deep connection between Portugal and its most iconic ingredient: salted cod. Surrounded by shelves that feel frozen in time, we uncover the stories of the old Portas de Santo Antão, the cod-fishing routes, and the role of bacalhau in the everyday life of the Portuguese. Here, we open the tasting experience with a selection of traditional cured meats paired with a glass of Port wine. Cities are layered. Their character emerges through their architecture, neighborhoods, and daily life. Lisbon in Layers City in Perspective Mapping the cityʼs evolution from medieval quarters to refined avenues: a foundation for your stay. The Art of Making Craft traditions live in the hands of those who practice them, in distinguished century-old shops. Private routes by tuk tuk or by car Writers & Cafés Cafés, streets, and meeting places that formed the intellectual surroundings of Portuguese literature. Food as Culture Markets, kitchens, and local producers frame the cityʼs food culture, with an optional cooking class.

Sacred Spaces Examining the role of Lisbonʼs churches, convents, and monasteries in shaping the city. Lisbon in Layers Collections in Context Guided museum visits placing works within their historical and cultural context. Private walking routes Jewish Heritage Through Lisbonʼs Jewish history, tracing presence and memory across the city. Lisbon becomes a playground of discovery, drawing ships, hunting for clues, and enjoying a pause for a picnic. Cafés & Writers Reading the city through its literary voices and cafés that nurtured its political and intellectual life.

Journeys on the Land From the Atlantic coast to medieval villages and limestone caves, Portugalʼs landscapes reveal the country beyond its cities.

Mysteries of Sintra Royal Dream Perched above the forests, Pena Palace expresses the romantic imagination of the 19th century, where architecture, myth, and fantasy meet. In the forests and hills of Sintra, palaces, legends, and symbols have inspired poets, mystics, and kings. Village of Legends In the village of Sintra, narrow streets and hidden corners still carry the legends that gave the mountain its mysterious reputation. A day journey from Lisbon, Cascais, or Sintra Language of Symbols At Quinta da Regaleira, gardens, tunnels, and the famous Initiation Well reveal a world shaped by symbols, secret passages, and ideas of transformation inspired by its creatorʼs imagination.

Sintra through Kids’ Eyes A Forest to Explore Hidden paths, lakes, and viewpoints make the forest and palace feel like a place of adventure. Sintra is a setting of discovery where kids can run through forests, meet animals, and explore stories that feel almost like fairy tales. Suitable for all ages. The Little Tram to the Ocean The historic tram connecting Sintra to the coast becomes a small journey through time. Children watch the scenery change from forest to ocean as the tram slowly reaches the seaside. A day journey from Lisbon, Cascais, or Sintra Life on the Farm At a traditional educational farm, children meet goats, chickens, rabbits, and other small animals. They can interact with the animals, learn aspects of rural life, and enjoy a slower pace in the countryside.

The Art of Escape, Sintra The Search for Meaning At Quinta da Regaleira, paths move through symbols, shadows, and discoveries. Nothing is immediate. Meaning takes time. Some places are not only visited. They are understood differently. This journey moves through three distinct perspectives: how we search, how we simplify, and how we compose. The Discipline of Simplicity At Convento dos Capuchos, everything is reduced to its simplest form. Stone, cork, and forest. A life defined by what is left out. A day journey from Lisbon, Cascais, or Sintra The Art of Form At Queluz National Palace, every element is placed with intention. Gardens, light and interiors reflect order, proportion, and control.
Traveling, to us, is about the experiences we live and the people we meet.

Echoes of Rome In the open terrain of the Alentejo, the ruins of São Cucufate evoke the Roman world that once cultivated these lands and introduced early wine traditions. Wine in Clay In the villages around Vidigueira, wine continues to be fermented in clay amphorae following a tradition that dates back to Roman times, preserved by local producers. River and Rice Fields One of Portugalʼs oldest inhabited towns, Alcácer do Sal stands above the Sado River, its medieval character overlooking wetlands and rice fields of the estuary. Journeys of Craft & Table Wineries, olive groves, and artisan workshops carry Portugalʼs traditions through the hands that shape them.

Craft of the Arrábida Hills Cheese Making in Azeitão At a historic cheese dairy, the making of the regionʼs celebrated cheese is explored from milk to maturation. Guests are invited to take part in the process, learning the techniques and shaping the cheese by hand. The Art of the Azulejo The craft behind Portugalʼs azulejos is introduced at this factory, using techniques preserved since the 16th century, with the opportunity to paint a tile. A Winemaking Legacy A six-generation family winery dating to 1834 shares its legacy through its House Museum and cellars. Periquita ages in oak and the oldest Moscatel de Setúbal rests in casks, some more than a century old. A day or multi-day journey from Lisbon In the villages around Arrábida, visitors step into the traditions of the regionʼs cheese, tiles, and wine.

Stories in Cork and Wine From Oak to Craft In the cork oak landscapes of Alentejo, the journey behind one of Portugalʼs most distinctive materials begins in the forest and continues to the workshop. Wine in Amphora At these historic estates, wines are still fermented in clay amphorae following ancient Roman traditions. The visit includes the cellars and a tasting of selected wines that embody the character of the Alentejo. Threads of Arraiolos In the hilltop town of Arraiolos, a centuries-old embroidery tradition gives life to the regionʼs distinctive wool tapestries. A workshop introduces the techniques behind these hand-stitched pieces. Alentejo traditions invite visitors to discover a world of cork forests, clay amphorae, and wool. Estates of Vine & Olive A Palace Among Vineyards At Casa de Mateus, one of Portugalʼs most remarkable Baroque residences, gardens, and vineyards reveal the cultural life of the Douro. A day or multi-day journey from Porto or Douro The Craft of Olive Oil Among the olive groves of a traditional Douro property, the owner shares the cultivation of the trees and the pressing process, before a tasting of freshly produced oil with ingredients prepared by his wife. Family Wineries of the Douro Here, meaningful wine moments happen at small family estates. Guided by the owners, visits may include picnics, tastings, or encounters with beehives. Over additional days, wineries with different traditions can be explored. Historic estates open their doors to guests, revealing why the Douro is renowned for wine and olive oil.

Journeys in Time Monasteries, medieval villages, and royal palaces trace the layers of Portugalʼs history across the centuries.

The Age of Discoveries The Monastery of the Discoveries The Jerónimos Monastery stands as one of Portugalʼs most remarkable examples of Manueline architecture. Its cloisters and church reflect the wealth and ambition of the maritime empire. In Belém, monuments and collections recall the age when Portuguese navigators opened the sea routes that connected the world. Masters of the Sea At the Maritime Museum, maps, instruments, and ships speak to the knowledge and ambition that allowed Portuguese navigators to cross the oceans. An afternoon by car in Lisbon A Tower at the Edge of the River The Belém Tower once guarded the entrance to Lisbonʼs harbor. Today it remains one of the most iconic symbols of Portugalʼs maritime history.

In the Templars’ Footsteps The Island Fortress Rising from a small island in the Tagus River, Almourol Castle stands as one of the most evocative fortresses associated with the Knights Templar in Portugal. In the Tagus Valley, fortresses and symbols still echo the legacy of the Knights Templar. Tomar, City of the Templars Founded in the 12th century by the Knights Templar, Tomar became one of the orderʼs most important strongholds in Europe and still carries the atmosphere of the city they once built. Symbols of the Order Built as a Templar stronghold, the Convent of Christ became the headquarters of their successors, the Order of Christ, preserving remarkable cloisters, symbols, and the celebrated Manueline window. A day journey from Lisbon

Paths of Faith Sanctuary of Devotion One of the most important pilgrimage destinations in the Catholic world, Fátima gathers pilgrims in prayer. Monasteries, sanctuaries, and coastal traditions reflect centuries of devotion in Portugal. A Monastery of Victory The Monastery of Batalha expresses the deep connection between faith and the founding of Portugal. A day journey from Lisbon Love Beyond Death Alcobaça houses the tombs of Pedro and Inês, whose tragic love story is one of Portugalʼs most powerful legends. Faith and the Sea In Nazaré, devotion to Our Lady of Nazaré has long accompanied the lives of fishermen and their families.

Origins of Portugal The Roman Capital One of Portugalʼs oldest cities, Braga traces its origins to the Roman settlement of Bracara Augusta. Today, its historic center reflects centuries of religious and cultural influence, where ancient streets, baroque churches, and traditional cafés echo the cityʼs long role in the countryʼs intellectual life. This journey connects two cities where the foundations of Portugal were laid. Birthplace of a Kingdom Regarded as the birthplace of Portugal, Guimarães preserves one of Portugalʼs most complete medieval centers. Its castle and the Ducal Palace recall the early years of the kingdom, when the first Portuguese king, Afonso Henriques, shaped the nation. A day journey from Porto

Trip Porto – Braga – 40 mi, 50 min We embark on a journey to Braga, one of Portugal's oldest cities, often called the "Portuguese Rome," with roots stretching back over 2,000 years. Founded by the Romans, Braga once rivaled Santiago de Compostela in both power and significance. Our first stop will be at the Bom Jesus do Monte Sanctuary, a masterpiece of faith and architecture, to visit this UNESCO site in Braga that invites reflection, beauty, and awe. Then our tour takes us through the historic center, with a stop at the iconic Café Vianna, which has been a cultural hub since its opening in 1871. Known as one of the country’s oldest cafés, it has welcomed a range of notable figures, including journalists, politicians, and writers like Eça de Queirós and Camilo Castelo Branco, who often referenced it in their works. After the break, we step into the Sé de Braga, Portugal’s oldest cathedral, where centuries of history, art, and devotion come alive in stone and silence. On our way, we’ll stroll through medieval streets and by the Santa Barbara Garden, a charming oasis in the heart of Braga where vibrant flowers bloom against the backdrop of ancient ruins. text: Trip Distance: Porto - Aveiro [48mi, 1h] From Porto to Aveiro, the road reveals a tapestry of rolling landscapes, vineyard-dotted hills, and coastal glimpses of the Atlantic. Passing through timeless villages and salt fields, the journey captures the essence of Portugal’s natural beauty and traditions. It concludes in elegant Aveiro, renowned for its canals, colorful moliceiro boats, and the delicate sweetness of ovos moles. MORNING B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 D O U R O T O A V E I R O As we arrive in Aveiro, we’ll have a quick stop at Costa Nova, on the seashore, for photos. With its iconic candy-striped houses, Costa Nova is a vibrant postcard come to life. This charming village, nestled between the calm of the Ria de Aveiro and the open sea, offers a delightful escape. It’s a place where timeless fishing traditions meet a joyful, colorful spirit. Time to savor the authentic flavors of Aveiro, where the local cuisine is a celebration of the sea. Enjoy a lunch centered on the freshest fish, from grilled sea bass (robalo) or sea bream (dourada) to a rich seafood rice (arroz de marisco). Or else, try a piglet sandwich, very typical in the area, for a quick lunch. LUNCH In Aveiro, step aboard a traditional moliceiro, a vessel with a history as rich as the city's own. These flat-bottomed boats, once used to harvest seaweed, now offer a serene and elegant passage along Aveiro's canals. As you glide past Art Nouveau buildings and the charming fishermen's quarter, you will witness the city's soul from a unique perspective, a timeless journey on its shimmering waterways.

text: Trip Distance: Aveiro - Óbidos [112 mi, 1h45] Leaving the coastal elegance of Aveiro behind, we embark on a journey inland to the heart of Portugal's medieval past. The drive to Óbidos is a scenic and relaxing one, a seamless transition from one unique landscape to another. As we approach, the magnificent walled town will emerge like a vision from a fairytale, and you will feel the air of history and romance that defines this exceptional place. This trip is a bridge between two distinct worlds—the coastal charm of Aveiro and the timeless, storybook beauty of Óbidos. AFTERNOON B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 A V E I R O T O Ó B I D O S Entering the gates of Óbidos is to step into a living history book. This perfectly preserved medieval town, enclosed by its ancient walls, invites you to wander its cobblestone streets and discover a world of timeless beauty. The air is filled with the scent of jasmine and the spirit of a bygone era, as you explore quaint shops and admire the traditional whitewashed houses adorned with vibrant bouganvillias. ÓBIDOS Trip distance: Óbidos - Lisbon [62 mi, 1h20] As we leave the timeless walls of Óbidos, our journey continues toward the heart of Portugal's vibrant capital, Lisbon. You'll soon be immersed in the city's lively atmosphere, ready to explore its historic hills, colorful neighborhoods, and monumental sights. We will take you to your hotel, allowing you to rest and refresh at your leisure. Ó B I D O S T O L I S B O N

text: Travel is not accumulation. It is interpretation. by BLU Costa Debbie’s Portugal Journey
Edition No. 03/2026 The Journey Portfolio
True luxury is a feeling of harmony, where every moment invites presence.

BLU, The House of Travel Curation Journeys in Cities Journeys on the Land Journeys by the Water Journeys of Craft & Table Journeys in Time From arrival to departure Contact 05 12 22 30 38 46 56 72 Contents

The House Travel is not accumulation. It is interpretation. We choose depth, context, presence. Luxury, to us, is time. Time to arrive, to understand, to feel. We curate moments that make sense and stay with you. BLU Costa The House of Travel Curation

The People Behind BLU Born and raised in Lisbon, Tiago brings a historian’s and architect’s eye to every journey. Adriana, a professor and a travel journalist, brings a storyteller’s sensibility to the details that matter. We believe travel is about the experiences we live and the people we meet along the way. We look forward to interpreting your moments with us. Adriana and Tiago

Every journey begins by understanding pace and what should remain. We do not assemble trips. We interpret them. Curation is the discipline of choosing what belongs and shaping how moments connect. Our work moves through five lenses: Journeys in Cities Journeys on the Land Journeys by the Water Journeys of Craft & Table Journeys in Time Not categories of tourism, but ways of shaping meaning. How We Curate

You are always understood We speak fluent English and we listen to you. Two guides on half- or full-day journeys One manages timing, access, and logistics. The other stays with you, guiding each visit. Less walking, more experiencing Stops are coordinated to reduce waiting, unnecessary walking and fatigue. Guided throughout, not just driven Each visit includes context and stories that deepen your understanding. A more personal way of traveling At times, we share moments such as a meal together, because the people you meet matter. Carefully chosen partners We work with trusted places and people, selected for their quality and genuine experiences they offer. Attentive service Inspired by Adrianaʼs background in travel journalism, our service reflects the standards of the worldʼs leading hotels. What Sets Us Apart

Every journey begins with a conversation. We listen carefully to understand what draws you to a region and how you prefer to travel. Some travelers simply wish to explore a city with a walking route. Others invite us to design and accompany their entire journey. From there, we begin selecting locations, encounters, and moments that connect meaningfully with your interests. We are here for you, whether you already know what you want or you simply have a vague idea. Our role is to interpret that intention and transform it into travel that feels memorable. How We Work with You

From Adriana Portugal invites a form of travel grounded in culture, landscape, and the continuity of everyday traditions. The journeys in the following pages represent locations we enjoy designing across the country, experiences that combine scenery, heritage, and encounters that remain long after the journey ends. They are simply starting points, ready to be adjusted around your interests and the time you wish to spend in each place. Welcome to BLU Costa — The House of Travel Curation.
Traveling, to us, is time. Time to arrive. Time to understand. Time to feel a place.
Journeys in Cities Historic quarters, cafés, and markets capture the daily life and culture of Portugalʼs cities beyond their monuments.

Cities are layered. Their character emerges through their architecture, neighborhoods, and daily life. Lisbon in Layers Lisbon in Perspective Mapping the cityʼs evolution from medieval quarters to refined avenues: a foundation for your stay. The Art of Making Craft traditions live in the hands of those who practice them, in distinguished century-old shops. Private routes by tuk tuk or by car Writers & Cafés Cafés, streets, and meeting places that formed the intellectual surroundings of Portuguese literature. Lisbon at the Table Markets, kitchens, and local producers frame the cityʼs food culture, with an optional cooking class. Sat, Mar 13

Sacred Spaces Examining the role of Lisbonʼs churches, convents, and monasteries in shaping the city. The Last Open Capital Tracing the intelligence networks, coded diplomacy, and silent negotiations that unfolded in WWII. Lisbon in Layers Collections in Context Guided museum visits placing works within their historical and cultural context. Private walking routes Jewish Heritage Through Lisbonʼs Jewish history, tracing presence and memory across the city. Symbols in Stone Reading the discreet presence of Masonic symbols embedded in façades and public spaces. Sat, Mar 13

The Age of Discoveries The Monastery of the Discoveries The Jerónimos Monastery stands as one of Portugalʼs most remarkable examples of Manueline architecture. Its cloisters and church reflect the wealth and ambition of the maritime empire. In Belém, monuments and collections recall the age when Portuguese navigators opened the sea routes that connected the world. Masters of the Sea At the Maritime Museum, maps, instruments, and ships speak to the knowledge and ambition that allowed Portuguese navigators to cross the oceans. An afternoon by car in Lisbon A Tower at the Edge of the River The Belém Tower once guarded the entrance to Lisbonʼs harbor. Today it remains one of the most iconic symbols of Portugalʼs maritime history. Sun, Mar 14
Curating, to us, is to choose what belongs and to leave the rest behind.

The Art of Escape, Sintra The Search for Meaning At Quinta da Regaleira, paths move through symbols, shadows, and discoveries. Nothing is immediate. Meaning takes time. Some places are not only visited. They are understood differently. This journey moves through three distinct perspectives: how we search, how we simplify, and how we compose. The Discipline of Simplicity At Convento dos Capuchos, everything is reduced to its simplest form. Stone, cork, and forest. A life defined by what is left out. A day journey from Lisbon, Cascais, or Sintra The Art of Form At Queluz National Palace, every element is placed with intention. Gardens, light and interiors reflect order, proportion, and control. Mon, Mar 15
Traveling, to us, is about the experiences we live and the people we meet.

The route north brings together locations that speak to Portugalʼs terrain and identity. The Lagoon City Along the lagoon of Aveiro, canals, colorful moliceiro boats, and Art Nouveau façades illustrate a city shaped by water and maritime traditions. Legacy in Porcelain Founded in 1824, Vista Alegre carries generations of craftsmanship and artistic dedication within one of Portugalʼs most distinguished porcelain traditions. A Village Frozen in Time Within its medieval walls, Óbidos preserves narrow streets, whitewashed houses, and a townscape that offers a glimpse into centuries of Portuguese history. Between Lisbon and Porto A day journey from Lisbon to Porto by car Tue, Mar 16

Tracing Porto's evolution through the monuments and neighborhoods that reflect centuries of trade, resilience, and change. Wine and Empire Crossing the Douro into Gaia, the journey follows the wine trade that connected Porto to the world, with a tasting in one of its historic Port wine cellars. Porto in Perspective Private journey by car Porto at the Table Bolhão Market introduces another side of Porto, where local producers and traditional flavors reflect the city's daily life and culinary heritage. The Historic Heart Porto's principal monuments, viewpoints, and neighborhoods provide a clear introduction to the city's history and character. Wed, Mar 17
Traveling, to us, is A memory that stays. A connection that is built. A longing to return.

Estates of Vine & Olive A Palace Among Vineyards At Casa de Mateus, one of Portugalʼs most remarkable Baroque residences, gardens, and vineyards reveal the cultural life of the Douro. A day or multi-day journey from Porto or Douro The Craft of Olive Oil Among the olive groves of a traditional Douro property, the owner shares the cultivation of the trees and the pressing process, before a tasting of freshly produced oil with ingredients prepared by his wife. Family Wineries of the Douro Here, meaningful wine moments happen at small family estates. Guided by the owners, visits may include picnics, tastings, or encounters with beehives. Over additional days, wineries with different traditions can be explored. Historic estates open their doors to guests, revealing why the Douro is renowned for wine and olive oil. Thu, Mar 18
Traveling, to us, is knowing why a place matters.

Origins of Portugal The Roman Capital One of Portugalʼs oldest cities, Braga traces its origins to the Roman settlement of Bracara Augusta. Today, its historic center reflects centuries of religious and cultural influence, where ancient streets, baroque churches, and traditional cafés echo the cityʼs long role in the countryʼs intellectual life. This journey connects two cities where the foundations of Portugal were laid. Birthplace of a Kingdom Regarded as the birthplace of Portugal, Guimarães preserves one of Portugalʼs most complete medieval centers. Its castle and the Ducal Palace recall the early years of the kingdom, when the first Portuguese king, Afonso Henriques, shaped the nation. A day journey from Porto Fri, Mar 19
From arrival to departure What remains for you is simple: to arrive, to be present, and to enjoy the journey.
Because when a journey is thoughtfully designed, travel becomes more than seeing, it becomes memory.

Supporting Your Journey Every journey begins long before the first step and stays with you long after you return. Whether you need help with a single reservation or the design of the entire trip, BLU can assist with the practical details. Airport and intercity transfers Chauffeur services Carefully chosen hotels Dining reservations Ticket acquisition Private access to monuments Private local guardians Special celebrations The pace of each day Everything is arranged so your time here feels easy and well cared for. Itʼs why we do what we do.

Transfers & Chauffeur Services We can arrange your arrival and departure transfers to ensure a smooth start and end to your journey. Professional drivers will meet you at the airport, train station, or other arrival points and accompany you comfortably to your hotel or next destination. Routes and timing are planned in advance so you can focus on the journey ahead. Private drivers can also be arranged throughout your stay for transfers between cities or for exploring the region at your own pace. Your arrival should feel easy from the start.

Hotel Curation BLU selects hotels for their character, location, and atmosphere: places that reflect your style and the identity of each region. From historic properties to discreet countryside estates and contemporary urban retreats, each accommodation is chosen with you, for you. Where you stay shapes how a location is experienced.

Dining Scene BLU recommends and secures reservations at restaurants that reflect local culture and culinary traditions: from refined gastronomy to small establishments known to locals. We also suggest the traditional dishes of each region, helping you discover the flavors that define each place. Your food preferences and dietary requirements are taken into account, and reservations are arranged in advance when necessary. A city is often best discovered at the table.

Tickets & Visit Planning Some visits and cultural events require advance reservations. Access to visits and cultural events as well as theatre, opera, concerts, and other events that may take place during your stay may be arranged. Transportation tickets, including train journeys between cities, can also be arranged when needed. We also advise on the best days and times to visit, how long to allow for each location, and whether a guided visit is recommended. This helps each visit fit naturally within the pace of your day. Coordinating access to visits and cultural events.

Private Access Some of the most remarkable monuments and museums reveal a different atmosphere when visited outside regular hours. Through special arrangements with cultural institutions, we can organize private access to selected sites before opening or after closing time. Without crowds and with time to observe details quietly, these visits allow a more intimate encounter with places that are usually experienced very differently. Availability depends on each institution and requires advance planning. Having a monument all to yourselves.

Private Local Guardians Certain places reveal themselves differently when explored with someone who knows their stories well. We call them Local Guardians. We collaborate with historians, cultural specialists, naturalists, and other knowledgeable local hosts who bring depth, context, and perspective to each visit. These encounters are arranged privately, allowing the experience to follow your pace and interests. Exploring settings with trusted local specialists.

Celebrations Some journeys carry a special reason: an anniversary, a proposal, a honeymoon, a birthday, or a moment that deserves to be celebrated. We help create these occasions with thoughtful arrangements that may include romantic dinners, flowers, private picnics, or other experiences designed around your wishes. The goal is simple: to make the moment feel personal and memorable. Marking meaningful moments.

Journey Design BLU designs travel around your interests and pace, shaping an itinerary that balances cultural depth and meaningful encounters. Your itinerary is designed with intention, leaving space for discovery and for simply being there. The result is moments that make sense and stay with you. Your journey should reflect who you are.

Travel Consultation Some travelers enjoy designing their own journeys and exploring possibilities along the way. At times, however, questions arise about logistics, recommendations, or how to shape the route. For those moments, we offer a one-hour dedicated video consultation to help refine your plans with a local perspective. Local insight through a dedicated video call. Video consultation: €50 per hour

Private Travel For those who prefer to travel with complete ease, the entire journey can be arranged with a private driver and guide. From arrival to departure, routes, timing, and visits are planned together so each day flows naturally. Your guide accompanies you throughout the trip, handling the details from check-in to parking, reservations, tickets, and unexpected situations, so you can simply enjoy the journey. Your journey supported from beginning to end.

How a BLU Journey Takes Shape 1. Conversation We begin by understanding what draws you to a location and how you prefer to travel. 4. Preparation Hotels, dining, visits, and logistics are confirmed so everything is ready before your arrival. From a wish to your return home 2. Interpretation We translate your interests into a journey concept, selecting settings and moments that belong together. 3. Journey Design Routes, visits, and pacing are shaped into an itinerary balancing discovery, rest, and meaningful moments. 5. The Journey Your time is free to focus on the journey.
Some journeys end. Others stay with us.
Until we meet. Adriana & Tiago

The River’s Pace Investment for 2 guests Group journey · Meeting point Avenida dos Aliados 8:45 – Boarding in Porto and departure along the Douro Valley. Breakfast and lunch are served on board as the river gradually reveals its changing landscapes, passing through the locks on the way to Pinhão. Faith and Tradition Sanctuary of Devotion One of the most important pilgrimage destinations in the Catholic world, Fátima gathers pilgrims in prayer. Portugal's story is written through faith, tradition, and the communities that have preserved both across generations. Beginning in Fátima, one of the world's great Marian shrines, and continuing to the medieval town of Óbidos, this journey offers an introduction to two places that continue to shape how Portugal is experienced and remembered. Town of Walls Encircled by medieval walls, Óbidos offers a glimpse into Portugalʼs past through its narrow streets, whitewashed houses, and preserved architecture. A day journey from Lisbon

09:00 - 14:00 Your day begins with a scenic drive from Lisbon to Fátima, where faith, history, and personal reflection come together. At the Sanctuary, we visit the Chapel of the Apparitions and the Basilica, with time to light a candle, browse the local religious shops, or simply pause and take in the atmosphere of one of the world's most important Marian pilgrimage sites before returning to Lisbon. CLASSIC JOURNEY

09:00 - 15:00 Beyond the Sanctuary, we continue to Aljustrel, the small village where the three shepherd children lived. Visiting their modest family homes offers a glimpse into the simplicity of their daily lives before the events of 1917. We pause for a light local snack, adding a relaxed moment to the day. EXTENDED JOURNEY

09:00 - 17:00 Leaving Fátima behind, we travel to the walled town of Óbidos. Once a royal gift to Portugal's queens, its medieval streets, whitewashed homes, and quiet squares offer time to wander, browse local shops, or enjoy a glass of the region's famous cherry liqueur before returning to Lisbon. Winding streets lead past majestic palaces and verdant gardens, where time seems to pause in an eternal twilight. With its romantic spirit and mystical atmosphere, Sintra invites you to uncover hidden treasures and lose yourself in its breathtaking beauty. M O R N I N G 09:00 - Departure from Lisbon to Sintra. 10:00 - We arrive at the Monserrate Palace, embarking on a journey to the romantic heart of Sintra. The palace rises like a fairy tale in stone, featuring Gothic, Indian, and Arab motifs. Discover a world of exoticism and beauty, where lush gardens and stunning architecture merge into a symphony of colors and shapes. Let yourself be carried away by the magic of this unique place, where nature and history intertwine in an unforgettable embrace. 11:30 - We proceed to the Regional Winery of Colares, the oldest cooperative winery in Portugal, founded in 1931, for a guided tour and wine tasting of the region, celebrated by personalities like Eça de Queiroz and Lord Byron.

BLUE COSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 hello@bluecostatravel.com | bluecostatravel.com B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel H I D D E N G E M S O F S I N T R A T A R D E 13:00 - We will have lunch at a typical Portuguese restaurant in the countryside, where the menu is still written in the old-fashioned way on a whiteboard. Here, traditional dishes like codfish, roasted lamb, and cuttlefish stew come steaming from the homemade kitchen. 15:00 - We continue our journey through the dense forest of Sintra, a place full of legends and mysticism. 15:30 - Visit to the Convent of the Capuchos, one of Portugal's best-kept secrets. Imagine a convent stripped of any luxury, built in the 16th century at the king's request, amidst rocks in the forest with walls covered in cork to protect the monks from the cold and damp. It is in this setting that we will reveal some of the region's mysteries.

text: From Adriana Lisbon is a city I never tire of. It reveals itself slowly, through light on the hills, the rhythm of its neighborhoods, and the way daily life continues quietly beside history. text: ALCOBAÇA MONASTERY One of Portugalʼs most important Gothic landmarks and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Founded in the 12th century, it reflects the power and influence of the Cistercian order. Its vast interior and pure architectural lines create a striking sense of scale and simplicity. It is also home to the iconic tombs of Pedro and Inês, one of Portugalʼs most enduring love stories. Within its monastic life, conventual sweets emerged, forming a lasting culinary tradition. Why it stays with you UNESCO heritage Portuguese Romeo & Juliet love story Traditional conventual desserts

text: BATALHA MONASTERY The Monastery of Batalha is a masterpiece of Gothic and Manueline archi-tecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Built to commemorate a decisive moment in Portugalʼs history, it stands as a symbol of national identity and ambition. Intricate stonework, soaring arches, and the Unfinished Chapels reveal remarkable artistic detail. A visit offers insight into the countryʼs history, architecture, and craftsmanship. text: TOMAR JEWISH LEGACY & TEMPLARS
Tomar: Jewish Legacy & Templars BLU Journey No. 505 Edition No. 01/2026 Journeys in Time
Traveling is... finding out that there is a part of us in everything, everywhere.

Tomar is a place where much was once present, and later forced into silence. This journey returns to that laye, recovering the Jewish presence that shaped the town through what still remains. Alongside it, the Templars and the Age of Expansion reveal how knowledge, power, and belief intersected here. I hope you feel the presence of those who lived here, and learn how their legacy extends beyond Portugal to the world. From Adriana
We are the memory we have. — JOSÉ SARAMAGO , Portuguese writer
A few favorite corners in Tomar to inspire you.

THE SYNAGOGUE The Synagogue of Tomar, the oldest in the Iberan Peninsula, has crossed centuries of change while preserving its essential form. Its central columns and balanced plan remain, even as its use shifted over time. What we read here is both structure and story, an enduring sense of order shaped by a past that was never entirely erased. Why it stays with you A space shaped around a shared center A history that didnʼt follow a straight line A presence that remains with no explanation

JEWISH QUARTERS The Jewish quarter of Tomar was organized along a single main street, where daily life and trade unfolded side by side. Its layout reflects a structured and closely connected community. Today, its simplicity remains, but the alignment of the streets and façades still reveals how this space once functioned. Why it stays with you The simplicity of the streets A place built for community What remains without being shown
Beauty lives in stone, light, and the patience of time.

CONVENT OF CHRIST At the Convent of Christ, different periods come together within a single complex. What began with the Templars continued under royal patronage, shaping a place that reflects both continuity and transformation. From the Charola to the cloisters, each space introduces a different scale and purpose, revealing how this site evolved over time. Why it stays with you The shift in scale and space Layers built across time Power expressed through form

Oh Portugal, who has sucked the milk of my ancient mothers... in you I grew, and in you I hoped to find a permanent home, but you turned into a stepmother who cast her children into the fire. — Samuel Usque - a 16th-century Portuguese author who wrote Consolation for the Tribulations of Israel, a foundational work of Sephardic literature.

text: Travel is not accumulation. It is interpretation. by BLU Costa Kara & Family Journey Summer 26
True luxury is a feeling of harmony, where every moment invites presence.

The House Travel is not accumulation. It is interpretation. We choose depth, context, presence. Luxury, to us, is time. Time to arrive, to understand, to feel. We curate moments that make sense and stay with you. BLU Costa The House of Travel Curation

The People Behind BLU Born and raised in Lisbon, Tiago brings a historian’s and architect’s eye to every journey. Adriana, a professor and a travel journalist, brings a storyteller’s sensibility to the details that matter. We believe travel is about the experiences we live and the people we meet along the way. We look forward to interpreting your moments with us. Adriana and Tiago

Every journey begins by understanding pace and what should remain. We do not assemble trips. We interpret them. Curation is the discipline of choosing what belongs and shaping how moments connect. Our work moves through five lenses: Journeys in Cities Journeys on the Land Journeys by the Water Journeys of Craft & Table Journeys in Time Not categories of tourism, but ways of shaping meaning. How We Curate

You are always understood We speak fluent English and we listen to you. Two guides on half- or full-day journeys One manages timing, access, and logistics. The other stays with you, guiding each visit. Less walking, more experiencing Stops are coordinated to reduce waiting, unnecessary walking and fatigue. Guided throughout, not just driven Each visit includes context and stories that deepen your understanding. A more personal way of traveling At times, we share moments such as a meal together, because the people you meet matter. Carefully chosen partners We work with trusted places and people, selected for their quality and genuine experiences they offer. Attentive service Inspired by Adrianaʼs background in travel journalism, our service reflects the standards of the worldʼs leading hotels. What Sets Us Apart

Every journey begins with a conversation. We listen carefully to understand what draws you to a region and how you prefer to travel. Some travelers simply wish to explore a city with a walking route. Others invite us to design and accompany their entire journey. From there, we begin selecting locations, encounters, and moments that connect meaningfully with your interests. We are here for you, whether you already know what you want or you simply have a vague idea. Our role is to interpret that intention and transform it into travel that feels memorable. How We Work with You

From Adriana Portugal invites a way of traveling shaped by the coast, with time spent between the sea, small towns, and life by the water. This journey focuses on beach settings and shared experiences, balancing time on the water, by the sand, and around the table. Each day is planned to feel easy and well-paced, with space to enjoy the surroundings and time together. Welcome to BLU Costa — The House of Travel Curation.
Traveling, to us, is time. Time to arrive. Time to understand. Time to feel a place.

Between Lisbon and the Algarve, the journey follows a gradual shift from sea-facing hills to wide, open land. text: Note from Adriana In Sintra, imagination comes easily. Forests hide paths. Castles seem drawn from stories. And every step invites curiosity. When we visit Sintra with children, we see the place differently. A walk through the forest becomes an adventure, ancient walls become castles waiting to be explored, and towers invite young minds to imagine distant kingdoms. Beyond the hills, simple moments in the countryside reveal another side of the landscape, one children understand instinctively, through curiosity and play. I hope that along these paths, they discover Sintra in a way that feels truly magical.

text: BEACH LUNCH At the edge of the Atlantic, Praia da Adraga offers a pause between cliffs, sea air, and the sound of waves reaching the sand. For children, the moment extends beyond the table, where the wide shore, the tide pools, and the calmness of the ocean invite curiosity long after lunch is finished. Why it stays with you Lunch beside the Atlantic A place once loved by a queen Time to play between sand and sea

text: AT THE TABLE LISBON
Lisbon at the Table BLU Journey No. 506 Edition No. 01/2026 Journeys of Craft & Table
Traveling is... giving time to scents and flavors.

And you, who hold the maritime empire, Where the sun rises on the eastern shore, You see the rich products of the Levant Flow into the Tagus in a endless stream — From Os Lusíadas (Canto X), immortalizing how black pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cloves flooded into the Casa da Índia at Lisbon's waterfront, reshaping global commerce.

CLASSIC JOURNEY Lisbon has always gathered the world around its table. Each taste reveals a story of journeys, connections, traditions and people, and how they became part of the city we know today. This is a walking journey through central Lisbon, with stops along the way and seated moments included. Comfortable walking shoes are recommended. Some tastings may vary with the season and availability at the places we visit. When they do, we will thoughtfully select an alternative that remains true to the spirit of the journey. text: Wine & Territory

Wine in Portugal is inseparable from landscape. Granite hills in the north, schist valleys in the Douro, Atlantic winds along the coast. A tasting in Lisbon becomes a journey through these regions, a sensory way to understand the country through its vineyards. This tasting offers three ways to approach that diversity. Wine Journey LX

A relaxed tasting of three Portuguese wines, presented with a brief introduction to the countryʼs main wine regions and grape varieties. A simple way to gain orientation and appreciation before dinner or an evening in the city. First Introduction Classic 3 wines from different Portuguese regions Introduction by a wine specialist Approx. 45 minutes Includes € 25 per person

A Deeper Understanding Extended A guided tasting of five wines, accompanied by a selection of Portuguese cheeses. The tasting moves across different regions and styles, allowing a clearer understanding of how geography and tradition shape Portuguese wines. 5 wines from distinct regions Portuguese cheese pairing Explanation of grape varieties and terroirs Approx. 1 hour Includes € 45 per person

Premium Wines & Regional Pairings Signature For those who enjoy wine with greater depth, this tasting focuses on five premium wines, selected for their character and provenance. From the cobblestone alleys of ancient cities like Lisbon and Porto to the medieval castles that dot the landscape, every corner of Portugal is a fascinating discovery. The warm hospitality of the Portuguese and the unique flavors of the delicious cuisine and award- winning wines complete the experience, making Portugal a destination that enchants in every aspect, touches the soul and inspires the imagination, providing precious memories. 19:30 - Transfer to VINUM Restaurant & Wine Bar VINUM’s dining experience brings the best of the north of Portugal and Basque country to the table The restaurant is nestled at Graham’s Port’s fully functioning 19thcentury cellars where generations of famous Port wines have been aged in over 3,200 oak barrels. Upon reaching Nazaré, a coastal gem known for its record-breaking waves and vibrant fishing traditions, you'll be greeted by dramatic cliffs and stunning ocean vistas. It's a journey that seamlessly combines cultural discovery with the allure of Portugal's natural beauty. Nazaré beach, with a mild climate and natural beauty, has one of the oldest traditions in Portugal linked to the arts of fishing. The long crescent-shaped beach, which is also the city's seafront, is known for its grandeur and the brightly colored awnings that decorate the white sand beach in contrast to the blue of the water. text: Trip Distance: Douro - Aveiro [95 mi, 1h40] From the undulating slopes of the Douro, where tradition and terroir meet, we embark on a journey of discovery towards Aveiro. The scenery will gracefully shift from the sun-drenched vineyards to the soft, coastal plains, a visual narrative that culminates in Aveiro's picturesque waterways and art nouveau façades. This seamless trip is a prelude to the city's unique allure, promising a captivating arrival. M O R N I N G B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 D O U R O T O A V E I R O As we arrive in Aveiro, we’ll have a quick stop at Costa Nova, on the seashore, for photos. With its iconic candy-striped houses, Costa Nova is a vibrant postcard come to life. This charming village, nestled between the calm of the Ria de Aveiro and the open sea, offers a delightful escape. It’s a place where timeless fishing traditions meet a joyful, colorful spirit. Time to savor the authentic flavors of Aveiro, where the local cuisine is a celebration of the sea. Enjoy a lunch centered on the freshest fish, from grilled sea bass (robalo) or sea bream (dourada) to a rich seafood rice (arroz de marisco). L U N C H Step aboard a traditional moliceiro, a vessel with a history as rich as the city's own. These flat- bottomed boats, once used to harvest seaweed, now offer a serene and elegant passage along Aveiro's canals. As you glide past Art Nouveau buildings and the charming fishermen's quarter, you will witness the city's soul from a unique perspective, a timeless journey on its shimmering waterways. Mysteries of Sintra BLU Journey No. 201 Edition No. 03/2026 Journeys on the Land
Sintra is not immediate. The visible is only the surface.

The House Travel is not accumulation. It is interpretation. We choose depth, context, presence. Luxury, to us, is time. Time to arrive, to understand, to feel. We curate moments that make sense and stay with you. BLU Costa The House of Travel Curation

The People Behind BLU Born and raised in Lisbon, Tiago brings a historian’s and architect’s eye to every journey. Adriana, a professor and a travel journalist, brings a storyteller’s sensibility to the details that matter. We believe travel is about the experiences we live and the people we meet along the way. We look forward to interpreting your moments with us. Adriana and Tiago

Every journey begins by understanding pace and what should remain. We do not assemble trips. We interpret them. Curation is the discipline of choosing what belongs and shaping how moments connect. Our work moves through five lenses: Journeys in Cities Journeys on the Land Journeys by the Water Journeys of Craft & Table Journeys in Time Not categories of tourism, but ways of shaping meaning. How We Curate

You are always understood We speak fluent English and we listen to you. Two guides on half- or full-day journeys One manages timing, access, and logistics. The other stays with you, guiding each visit. Less walking, more experiencing Stops are coordinated to reduce waiting, unnecessary walking and fatigue. Guided throughout, not just driven Each visit includes context and stories that deepen your understanding. A more personal way of traveling At times, we share moments such as a meal together, because the people you meet matter. Carefully chosen partners We work with trusted places and people, selected for their quality and genuine experiences they offer. Attentive service Inspired by Adrianaʼs background in travel journalism, our service reflects the standards of the worldʼs leading hotels. What Sets Us Apart

Every journey begins with a conversation. We listen to understand what draws you to a place and how you prefer to travel. Some travelers seek a single day well designed. Others ask us to shape and accompany an entire journey. From there, we select the places, encounters, and pacing that belong together. Whether your ideas are clear or still taking form, our role is to interpret them. How We Work with You

From Adriana Sintra asks for time. Not to see more, but to notice differently. In Sintra, meaning lives in layers, in symbols, in silence, in what is left unsaid. There is a quiet tension here between nature and imagination, between what is built and what is believed. This journey moves through that space.

Today is the happiest day of my life. I know Italy, Sicily, Greece, and Egypt, and I have never seen anything, anything, to equal the Pena. It is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen. — Richard Strauss, German composer
A few favorite corners in Sintra to inspire you.

PENA PALACE Pena resists a single reading. Raised above the forest, it reflects a moment when imagination and power converged deliberately. Color and stone. Myth and intention. A palace built to hold contradiction Not to impress, but to be understood. Why it stays with you Romanticism at full expression Harmony found in contrast An architecture of contrasts

CARRIAGE RIDE Along the winding paths of Pena Park, a carriage ride brings a gentler pace to the forest. The sound of hooves on the path. The slow movement through tall trees. The landscape begins to shift. The forest and the hills create a moment that seems to pause time Why it stays with you The steady pace of the carriage A forest seen differently A quieter way through the landscape
Beauty lives in repetition.

SINTRA OLD TOWN The village moves at its own pace. Streets slip into one another, corners hold more than they show. Palaces rise in the distance, but here, meaning lives in details, in shadows, in textures. You move through them, and they stay just out of reach. Why it stays with you Quiet disorientation What remains beyond view Streets that conceal as much as they reveal

Sintra is the place where the silence is not an absence of sound, but a presence of secrets. Every stone is a word of an ancient language that we have forgotten how to speak. — Fernando Pessoa, Portuguese poet

We begin the day in Sintra, a picturesque village at the foot of the mountain that shares its name. Its unique character led UNESCO to create a special category when designating it as a World Heritage Site — the “Cultural Landscape” — recognizing not only the town’s architectural treasures but also the natural beauty of the surrounding mountains. With its imposing turrets and stunning panoramic views, the palace is a popular tourist destination, offering visitors a fascinating experience amid stunning scenery. 11:00 - We head down to the city center, to wander through Sintra’s enchanting medieval alleys and savor its iconic pastry, once a royal favorite. text: ESTORIL Estoril carries a more discreet kind of glamour. Arrival in Porto Transfer from Airport to Hotel Check-in at hotel M O R N I N G B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 We head to the riverside to enjoy lunch with the most famous view of Porto. In the afternoon, we explore Porto's historical district, a city shaped by its prosperous port wine trade that flourished in the 18th century, especially with the arrival of English merchants who established renowned companies like Sandeman and Offley, bypassing intermediaries. Unlike Lisbon, which suffered significant damage from the 1755 earthquake, Porto remained intact, allowing its rich heritage to be beautifully preserved. L U N C H & A F T E R N O O N P O R T O - A R R I V A L & C I T Y T O U R Free E V E N I N G

P O R T O - B R A G A - G U I M A R Ã E S - P O R T O Trip Porto – Braga – 40 mi, 50 min We embark on a journey to Braga, one of Portugal's oldest cities, often called the "Portuguese Rome," with roots stretching back over 2,000 years. Founded by the Romans, Braga once rivaled Santiago de Compostela in both power and significance. Our tour takes us through the historic center, with a stop at the iconic Café Vianna, which has been a cultural hub since its opening in 1871. Known as one of the country’s oldest cafés, it has welcomed a range of notable figures, including journalists, politicians, and writers like Eça de Queirós and Camilo Castelo Branco, who often referenced it in their works. MORNING Trip Braga – Guimarães - 15 mi, 30 min Our journey continues to Guimarães, known as the birthplace of Portugal, where the nation's first king, Afonso Henriques, was born. Here, we will visit two of the city's most iconic landmarks: the historic Guimarães Castle and the majestic Ducal Palace. B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel LUNCH We'll enjoy lunch at a traditional restaurant in the iconic Largo da Oliveira, located in the heart of the historic center. This is also the perfect chance to savor one of the city’s beloved desserts, Toucinho do Céu, a local delicacy. BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628

We will stroll around its well-preserved historic center, a UNESCO World Heritage site, where we'll find narrow cobblestone streets, traditional squares, and a captivating blend of medieval and modern architecture. Guimarães offers a unique journey through Portugal’s past in a setting that feels timeless. AFTERNOON Trip Guimarães – Porto – 40 mi, 50 min We return to Porto in the late afternoon. B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel EVENING Free BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 P O R T O - B R A G A - G U I M A R Ã E S - P O R T O

DOURO: CASA DE MATEUS, OLIVE OIL FARM MORNING Viagem: 60 mi, 1h20 min We set off to explore the Douro region, beginning with a visit to Vila Real and the stunning Fundação da Casa de Mateus. Built in the early 18th century, the Mateus Palace is surrounded by exquisite gardens and is renowned as one of Portugal's finest examples of Baroque architecture. This magnificent estate includes the main house, chapel, and winery, along with historic gardens, orchards, vineyards, and woodland. Inside, you’ll find intricately carved wooden ceilings, period furniture, 17th- and 18th- century paintings, silverware, ceramics, and a library housing a rare edition of *Os Lusíadas*. Our visit includes a guided tour of the Casa de Mateus, offering a deeper look into its rich history and collections. B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628

Lunch at a traditional restaurant. LUNCH We’ll take a scenic drive through some of the region’s most picturesque villages before embarking on one of the trip’s highlights: a visit to a traditional olive oil mill. Here, we'll witness the artisanal production of olive oil, descending the property’s slopes in a jeep to explore the cultivation of centuries-old olive trees. Along the way, the owner will share fascinating insights and amusing stories about the land. To complete the experience, we’ll enjoy a tasting of freshly produced olive oil, paired with other homegrown ingredients lovingly prepared by his wife. Trip Douro - Porto: 75 mi, 1h30 B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel EVENING Free AFTERNOON BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 DOURO: CASA DE MATEUS, OLIVE OIL FARM

DOURO: WINERIES & DOURO CRUISE FULL DAY Viagem: 170 mi, 4h A road trip from Porto to the Douro Valley is a journey through one of Portugal's most stunning landscapes. As you leave the city behind, the road winds through rolling hills, terraced vineyards, and alongside the shimmering Douro River. The valley, famous for its Port wine production, offers breathtaking views at every turn. Along the way, we will pass by charming villages, visit historic wineries for tastings, and take in the beauty of this UNESCO World Heritage site, making it an unforgettable scenic adventure. We’ll visit two exceptional wineries, where you’ll dive into the art and tradition of Port wine production. As you explore the cellars and vineyards, you’ll uncover the rich history behind each bottle, and indulge in tastings that bring the region’s world-renowned flavors to life. Before heading back to Porto, we'll experience the breathtaking beauty of the Douro Valley from a whole new angle, gliding along the Douro River on a serene cruise. As we sail between the terraced vineyards and rolling hills, you'll have the chance to fully immerse yourself in the region's tranquil landscapes, making for a perfect, unforgettable finale to the day. text: PASSEIO DAS VIRTUDES Tucked behind the Jardim das Virtudes, this tiered stone terrace is more than just a viewpoint; it is the cityʼs communal living room. Itʼs a place where the grandeur of granite architecture meets the raw, shimmering beauty of the Douro, inviting you to slow down, sit on the grass, and simply exist in the moment. To visit Virtudes is to witness Porto at its most authentic: unpretentious, breathtaking, and bathed in golden light. Why it stays with you The feeling of arriving nowhere in particular The city below in slow movement Sunset without spectacle

text: CAPELA DAS ALMAS Capela das Almas turns an ordinary street corner into something unmistakably Porto. Covered in thousands of blue-and-white tiles, the chapel brings together devotion, craftsmanship, and everyday movement, standing between cafés, shops, and the rhythm of the city around it. More than a monument, it feels woven into daily life. Familiar to locals, yet capable of making even a brief passage through the street slow down for a moment. text: ESCOVARIA BELMONTE Stepping into Escovaria Belmonte is like stepping through a portal into a Porto that refuses to be rushed. This workshop has been handcrafting brushes since 1927, proving that true quality is timeless. It is one of the few remaining artisanal brush factories in Europe where the scent of wood shavings and natural fibers still fills the air. Here, a simple tool is elevated to a work of art, crafted with a level of precision and soul that mass production simply cannot replicate. Why it stays with you The Tactile Time Capsule Witnessing Living History Craft still rooted in everyday life

text: D A Y T R I P : P O R T O - N A Z A R É - Ó B I D O S - L I S B O N 09:30 - Check out from the hotel in Porto. Driving from Porto to Nazaré is a scenic adventure that takes you through the diverse landscapes of Portugal. As you leave Porto’s historic charm behind, the route unfolds with views of lush countryside, charming villages, and rolling hills. Upon reaching Nazaré, a coastal gem known for its record-breaking waves and vibrant fishing traditions, you'll be greeted by dramatic cliffs and stunning ocean vistas. It's a journey that seamlessly combines cultural discovery with the allure of Portugal's natural beauty. Nazaré beach, with a mild climate and natural beauty, has one of the oldest traditions in Portugal linked to the arts of fishing. The long crescent-shaped beach, which is also the city's seafront, is known for its grandeur and the brightly colored awnings that decorate the white sand beach in contrast to the blue of the water. This is the beach in Portugal where fishing traditions are most colorful and it is not uncommon to come across fishmongers who still wear the seven skirts, as tradition dictates. It looks like a city created for a medieval film, completely walled with a castle built by the Arabs in the 13th century, one of the Seven Wonders of Portugal. Das ruelas de paralelepípedos das cidades antigas, como Lisboa e Porto, aos castelos medievais que pontilham a paisagem, cada canto de Portugal é uma descoberta fascinante. A hospitalidade calorosa dos portugueses e os sabores únicos da gastronomia saborosa e os vinhos premiados completam a experiência, tornando Portugal um destino que encanta em todos os aspectos, toca a alma e inspira a imaginação, proporcionando memórias preciosas. Vamos embarcar em uma jornada de descoberta que promete momentos inesquecíveis e inspiração constante. M A N H Ã B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 D I A 0 4 - S I N T R A - C A B O D A R O C A - C A S C A I S Vamos percorrer os vilarejos da Serra de Sintra até o restaurante para nosso almoço, um lugar típico onde o menu diário é escrito na lousa branca como é feito há dezenas de anos. A L M O Ç O Iniciamos o dia em Sintra. Lindíssima vila no sopé da Serra do mesmo nome, as suas características únicas fizeram com que a UNESCO ao classificá-la como património mundial fosse obrigada a criar uma categoria específica para o efeito - a de "paisagem cultural" - que desta forma considera tanto a riqueza natural como o património construído na vila e na serra. A Serra de vegetação luxuriante está inserida no Parque Natural Sintra-Cascais. Faremos um passeio de carro pelas ruas de Sintra e seguimos pela lindíssima estrada pela Serra de Sintra, passando por paisagens de serra e mar.

Continuamos até o Cabo da Roca, o ponto mais ocidental da Europa Continental. Situado na latitude 38º 47´ Norte e na longitude 9º 30´ Oeste, o Cabo da Roca é uma coordenada importante para quem navega ao longo da costa, sendo o ponto mais ocidental do continente europeu continental. T A R D E B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 N O I T E Noite livre. D I A 0 5 - A Z E I T Ã O - A R R Á B I D A - S E T Ú B A L Nossa primeira parada é em Azeitão. Foi sobretudo a partir do século XV que Azeitão ganhou prestígio, com a instalação de famílias nobres. As quintas, os palácios e as fontes que se espalham por este território são testemunhos desses tempos. Hoje, vale pela paz bucólica, pelo peso da História patente em cada edifício, pela simpatia dos habitantes e, em particular, pelas experiências gastronómicas que oferece. M A N H Ã B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 A seguir, visitamos a Casa Museu da vinícola José Maria da Fonseca, onde a empresa José Maria da Fonseca foi fundada em 1834. No final, vocês provarão alguns dos vinhos produzidos pela José Maria da Fonseca. O percurso pela Casa-Museu é acessível e inicia-se com uma breve explicação sobre a história da empresa familiar já na sexta geração, seguindo-se a visita às antigas adegas: a Adega da Mata e a Adega dos Teares Novos, onde estagia, entre outros, o vinho Periquita, e a Adega dos Teares Velhos, onde repousam os mais antigos Moscatéis de Setúbal, alguns dos quais autênticas relíquias com mais de 100 anos. Começamos com uma visita à Fábrica de Azulejos, para conhecer o processo de fabricação artesanal de um dos patrimônios nacionais de Portugal, o azulejo. Após a visita, vocês terão a oportunidade de colocar a mão na massa, ou nos pincéis, e pintar o seu próprio azulejo e levá-lo para casa como recordação.

Próxima parada é uma das estradas mais bonitas de Portugal, a da Serra da Arrábida, um paraíso natural de Portugal. Com paisagens deslumbrantes de colinas cobertas de vegetação exuberante, enseadas escondidas e praias de águas cristalinas, a Serra da Arrábida é um refúgio de tranquilidade e beleza. Restaurante típico em Setúbal. A culinária de Setúbal é uma celebração dos sabores locais, especialmente os frutos do mar frescos e os vinhos da região, experiência deliciosa que combina a tradição culinária portuguesa com os ingredientes frescos e o toque único desta encantadora cidade costeira. B L U C O S T A Bespoke Travel BLUCOSTA Bespoke Travel | +351 91 578 4212 | +351 938 567 628 A L M O Ç O Vamos saborear a culinária local que se destaca pelos sabores frescos do mar, refletindo a tradição piscatória da vila. Pratos simples, como peixe grelhado e caldeirada; o marisco, especialmente amêijoas e percebes, é amplamente apreciado. Após o check-out no hotel, seguimos para Nazaré, Portugal, onde falésias dramáticas se erguem sobre um mar indomável e tradições antigas ganham vida. Passearemos por ruas acolhedoras, e vamos saborear a culinária local rica em peixes e mariscos frescos, enquanto se maravilham com vistas espetaculares do oceano. Uma experiência que captura a essência da natureza e a alma da cultura portuguesa M A N H Ã D I A 0 6 - L I S B O A - N A Z A R É - P O R T O

Passearemos pela vila. A praia da Nazaré, de clima ameno e com uma beleza natural, tem das mais antigas tradições de Portugal ligadas às artes da pesca. O longo areal em forma de meia-lua, e que é também a frente de mar da cidade, é conhecido pela sua grandeza e pelos toldos de cores vivas que decoram a praia de areia branca em contraste com o azul da água. Esta é a praia de Portugal onde as tradições da pesca são mais coloridas e não é raro cruzarmo-nos com as peixeiras que ainda usam as sete saias, como manda a tradição. No entanto, a memória da heroica resistência da população às forças napoleônicas durante a invasão no início do século XIX prevalece. Não podemos deixar de provar os indecentes doces de São Gonçalo. M A N H Ã Viagem: 45 km, 40 min Continuamos até Vila Real para visitar a magnífica Fundação da Casa de Mateus. Edificado na primeira metade do séc. XVIII, o Palácio Mateus rodeado de belos jardins inseridos numa vasta quinta é considerado um dos expoentes máximos da arquitetura barroca em Portugal. Um conjunto arquitetônico composto pela Casa, Capela e Casas da Adega, de um perímetro composto por jardins históricos, pomares, vinhas e zona de bosque e de um extenso espólio constituído por arquivo, biblioteca e coleções museológicas. Da sua decoração interior ressaltam os tetos em madeira ricamente trabalhada, o mobiliário de diferentes épocas, pintura dos séculos XVII e XVIII, objetos de prata, cerâmica e uma biblioteca onde avulta uma edição notável de Os Lusíadas. From Adriana In Sintra, imagination comes easily. Forests hide paths. Castles seem drawn from stories. And every step invites curiosity. When we visit Sintra with children, we see the place differently. A walk through the forest becomes an adventure, ancient walls become castles waiting to be explored, and towers invite young minds to imagine distant kingdoms. Beyond the hills, simple moments in the countryside reveal another side of the landscape, one children understand instinctively, through curiosity and play. I hope that along these paths, they discover Sintra in a way that feels truly magical.

In the woods of Sintra, the shadows are thick and green like the bottom of the sea. A child walking here does not walk on earth, but on a carpet of legends, where the silence is made of stories waiting to be told. — Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen in Christmas Nights
A few favorite corners across Sintra hills to inspire you.

High above Sintraʼs forest stands a palace that seems imagined rather than built. Turrets, terraces, and bright colors appear through the trees as the paths climb slowly toward the hilltop. For children, the walk through the park feels like entering a story where every turn reveals something unexpected, inviting young explorers to imagine kingdoms, guardians, and secret passages hidden among the gardens. PENA PALACE Why it stays with you Paths that feel like an adventure Castles that awaken imagination Views that make the world feel wide

CARRIAGE RIDE Along the winding paths of Pena Park, a carriage ride brings a gentle rhythm to the forest. The sound of hooves on the path and the slow movement through tall trees allow children to notice the landscape differently. From the carriage, the journey itself becomes part of the discovery, where the forest, the hills, and the palace above create a moment that feels both peaceful and quietly exciting. Why it stays with you The steady rhythm of the carriage A forest seen from a different pace A journey that feels like a story

THE HILLSIDE LINE The tram runs along the hills around Sintra, following a line framed by tall trees and open stretches of land. It moves steadily, the sound of the rails marking the way, as the view shifts between forest and small clearings. For children, it feels like a ride through a hidden path, where each turn brings something new to notice. Why it stays with you A ride that feels like an adventure Trees that frame every moment The simple joy of moving through it all

BEACH LUNCH At the edge of the Atlantic, Praia da Adraga offers a pause between cliffs, sea air, and the sound of waves reaching the sand. Nearby, a small restaurant long known as one of Queen Améliaʼs favorite places welcomes travelers with simple seafood and views over the beach. For children, the moment extends beyond the table, where the wide shore, the tide pools, and the calmness of the ocean invite curiosity long after lunch is finished. Why it stays with you Lunch beside the Atlantic A place once loved by a queen Time to play between sand and sea
Beauty lives in small encounters.

DONKEY RIDE In the quiet countryside beyond the hills, a walk with donkeys becomes a small adventure. With gentle steps and patient companions, children quickly learn how to guide them along the path, discovering that curiosity and kindness lead the way. Between laughter, small discoveries, and the open countryside, the moment becomes less about riding and more about forming a quiet friendship along the way. Why it stays with you Meeting gentle companions Small adventures along the path A countryside moment to remember

ANIMALS ENCOUNTER In the open countryside, children step into a world where animals are part of everyday life. Donkeys, ponies, goats, sheep, rabbits, and curious chickens gather around as small hands offer food and gentle attention. Between feeding, brushing, and short rides through the fields, the encounter becomes a joyful way to discover how animals live alongside people. Why it stays with you Meeting animals up close Learning care through simple gestures Moments of curiosity and laughter

CHALET CONDESSA Hidden within the forested hills of Sintra stands a small chalet that feels almost like a secret discovered along the path. Inside, intricate patterns cover the walls and ceilings, each room revealing the care and imagination of those who once lived here. For parents, it offers a glimpse into a romantic chapter of Sintraʼs history; for children, the house can feel like something from a story, where every doorway invites a little curiosity. Why it stays with you A house filled with delicate details Stories hidden in every room A quiet corner of Sintra

CORK CONVENT The Convent of the Capuchos is a place of quiet retreat, shaped by simplicity and reflection. Built in the 16th century, the convent was designed for a humble life. Stone, wood, and cork replace ornament, creating spaces where comfort gives way to contemplation. Here, silence becomes part of the experience — a rare moment to pause, breathe, and connect with a deeper sense of calm. The silence of the forest Its one-of-a-kind cork architecture The feeling of humility and presence Why it stays with you

SINTRA OLD TOWN Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the old town of Sintra unfolds through everyday life. Narrow streets and small squares shape a steady rhythm, where the past feels present without calling attention to itself. As you wander, traces of time appear quietly — in the streets, the buildings, and the way life continues. The charm on its medieval streets The contrast of layers The picturesque palaces on the hills Why it stays with you

CABO DA ROCA Cabo da Roca is a place where the land seems to pause before meeting the ocean, standing at the westernmost point of continental Europe. For centuries, this edge of land was believed to be the end of the known world. Even today, that feeling remains — a quiet awareness of distance, depth, and possibility. Here, wind, sea, and sky take the lead, offering a moment of presence where words feel unnecessary. The feeling of standing at the edge The openess of the horizon Its raw beauty Why it stays with you

CASCAIS Cascais carries the ease of a seaside retreat, shaped by time and the pull of the ocean.
